Inline Attachment Images

Gmail exposes inline image attachments as MIME parts with a Content-ID header, referenced in the HTML body as cid: URLs rather than http(s) URLs. This is a very common newsletter pattern (screenshots pasted directly into an email client) and is currently dropped outright because embed logic only accepts src values starting with "http".

Text after the inline image, to confirm the rest of the body survives even when the cid: image cannot yet be resolved.
